subject: Post-call: scope for parallel sessions, connection pooling, and pilot ratecards
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@finledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: parallel sessions and connection-pool sizing

Hi Sam / Olivia —

Thanks for taking the time this morning. Quick written recap from our call and the open items we discussed so both sides have the same scope for the pilot: 

- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 350ms for chat inference (typical seq length ~512).
- Throughput: target baseline 150 requests/sec sustained during peak 10-minute windows, with planned burst capacity to 500 RPS for short spikes.
- Concurrency model and pooling: you prefer persistent HTTP/2 clients with multiplexing (web clients vs server-side workers TBD). Initial sizing proposed: 50 persistent connections per region, with up to 10 concurrent streams each (effective parallel requests ~500).
- Streaming: token-level streaming required for chat; Redwood will stream incremental tokens over HTTP/2. Max idle stream timeout ~60s.
- Failure/fallback: when connection limits are hit, fallback policy should route to a lower-throughput model variant (we discussed a managed fallback).

Action items for Redwood (assigned to me/Ben):
1) Produce a 3-month pilot rate estimate and a temporary connection-pool quota increase request (quota bump for connection_count and burst tokens).
2) Share recommended SDK settings for HTTP/2 pool sizing, keepalive, and client-side backoff.
3) Draft a short mutual action plan (pilot acceptance criteria, load-test dates, cutover checklist).

Action items for FinLedger (assigned to Sam/Olivia):
- Confirm average tokens per request (you estimated ~320 tokens) and expected requests/day distribution (peak windows).
- Confirm whether web clients will keep long-lived streaming connections or open short-lived streaming sessions (this affects pool sizing).

Attachment: rate_estimate_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Ben — can you coordinate with infra to see what a temporary quota jump looks like for the pilot (50% bump on connection_count and a burst token allowance)?

Thanks,

-- 
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sam Reynolds <sam@finledger.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia@finledger.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: parallel sessions and connection-pool sizing

Thanks Stephanie — good notes. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Tokens: confirmed average ~320 tokens/request for our chat messages, sometimes up to 700 for legal summaries. We'll send a short CSV with a sample distribution by EOD.
- Burst window: on the call I mentioned a 5-minute burst window (not 1-2 minutes) — the longer window matters for our front-end behavior during market opens. If you can size for 5 minutes that would be safer.
- Clients: web clients will generally re-use HTTP/2 short-lived streams (they're not always long-lived websockets). Server-to-server workers will keep longer-lived connections.

We appreciate Redwood's willingness to do a temporary quota bump for the pilot; let us know what you need from our side.

Sam Reynolds
Head of Platform Engineering, FinLedger
